analysis.title: Duttenhoefer's Daily 05.10.2026
key_insights: S&P 500 rose 73bps to 7723 (+13% YTD) after weaker NFP (29k vs consensus 90k). Probability of an October Fed hike fell below 20%. Nasdaq reached new all-time highs despite higher yields.
US 10-year yield unchanged at 5.27% and US 30-year mortgage rates are above 7.3%. OAT/Bund spread is 160bps, the widest since the 2011 eurozone debt crisis.
Brent is back at $102 on Iran headlines. Gold is $4130, Bitcoin $85k, and EUR/USD is below 1.12 for the first time since May 2025. Nvidia market cap touched $5.7tn.

US x Iran: the Pentagon confirmed deployment of a third carrier strike group (USS Theodore Roosevelt) and 10k additional troops to the Persian Gulf. Tehran is preparing a broader response to any renewed large-scale US attack.

Hedge funds: US L/S net leverage fell for a third straight week to 46.4%, the lowest since April 2025 and near the 2nd percentile of 5-year lows. Europe saw its largest % net buying in over five years.

US data center construction spending rose 73.2% y/y in August to $85bn, while total US construction spending fell 1.7% y/y. GS says the buildout supports demand for power infrastructure and specialist construction trades.

Q3 US earnings season starts next week. Consensus expects S&P 500 EPS growth of 27% y/y. AI infrastructure spending accounts for over 50% of S&P 500 EPS growth, alongside hyperscaler capex growth of 116%. Median S&P stock EPS growth is about 9% (vs 14% in Q2).
The top 10 contributing stocks are expected to account for 68% of S&P 500 earnings growth in 3Q26 (vs 48% in 2Q26). Micron and Nvidia together account for 34% of index growth.
Fed: GS thinks an October hike is unlikely and sees a strong chance the FOMC concludes additional hikes are unnecessary.

Amazon is added to the Conviction List into Q3. Analyst Eric sees upside from above-Street AWS growth and margins, the orchestration layer, a ~$70bn Physical AI opportunity and digital advertising strength, despite the agentic commerce debate.

Gold: major discoveries remain scarce. S&P Global counts 9 deposits found since 2020 that reached the 2m-ounce threshold. The average major find holds 4.3m ounces (7.3m in the 2010s) and discovery-to-production now takes 16 years.
EU Conviction List adds Solaria, Straumann, Scout24 and IMCD, and removes Naturgy, Norsk Hydro and Smith & Nephew.

GS's GSXUBOND basket (48 stocks) is an equity expression of a long-duration view, with RSI below 30 and forward dividend yield above 4%. On five prior occasions with those conditions, 1-month returns averaged +2.7% (80% hit rate) and 3-month returns averaged +5.9%.

DRAM sentiment indicator for September is moderately positive. DDR5/DDR4 pricing continued to rise, and server ODM monthly revenue growth reached a record +130% y/y. Memory and HBM pricing expectations have been reset and have started to recover.

European equities have underperformed other regions since August. EPS momentum is positive and FCF yield is 5.5% vs 3.5% for the US. GS stays overweight Technology, Banks, Renewables, Defense and Capital intensive.
Market breadth: the S&P 500 is 2% from its all-time high while the median stock is 17% below its high, the weakest breadth since the dot-com bubble.
More than $1.5tn has flowed into US-listed ETFs this year, passing last year's record in three quarters. GS expects flows above $2tn in 2026.
